Vs.

full_judgment:
2. Briefly stated, the facts are that the respondent no. 1 Sonali Bank obtained a decree against the present petitioners in Money Suit No. 7/92 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Jhenaidah for realisation of Tk. 75, 94,994/-. The respondent bank put the decree in execution being Money Execution Case No. 49/93. Ultimately the execution case was fixed on 2.4.2000 for taking steps by the decree holder and on the said date the respondent no. 1 bank filed an application under Order 21 Rule 38 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for detaining the judgment-debtor-petitioner in civil prison alleging them due to the conspiracy made by the judgment-debtor the decretal property could not be sold and the intending bidder did not appear and therefore the judgment-debtor is required to be detained in the civil prison. The learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat after hearing the learned Advocate of the decree-holder passed the impugned order dated 12.4.2000 for committing the judgment-debtors to the civil prison for one month. It is against that order the petitioner obtained the present Rule. 

 4. It is contended by Mr. Abdul Jabbar that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has no authority under the Rules i.e. Rule 37 and Rule 40 of Order 21 C.P.C. to make any order for detention in civil prison without is-suing notice calling upon the judgment-debtor to show cause why he or they should not be committed to the civil prison for non-payment of the decretal dues and for creating any hindrance or effecting delay to execution of the decree for realisation of the money. Pointing out rule 40 he has argued .that according to the Rules the executing Court must issue a notice calling upon the judgment-debtor to appear before the Court on a day specified in the notice and then when the judgment-debtor appears before the Court or is brought before the Court after being arrested the Court shall proceed to hear the decree-holder and take all such evidence as may be produced by the decree-holder in support of the application for execution and the Court shall then give the judgment-debtor an opportunity of showing cause why the judgment-debtor should not be committed to the civil prison. Having not complied with the mandatory provision of the rules the Artha Rin Adalat has committed gross illegality. 

 5. Mr. A.B.M. Bayezid, the learned Advocate for the respondent finds it difficult to support the order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Although in the case of Agrani Bank Vs. Artha Rin Adalat reported in 55 DLR 389 in which one of us was a party it was held that if any mistake is committed in passing any order under the provisions of C.P.C. and in applying the provisions of the Code in execution proceeding, such mistake palpable or apparent or gross in nature may be corrected in appropriate case to do justice and undo injustice by the Court having civil jurisdiction by exercising its power both under sections 115(1) and 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But in the instant case seemingly the impugned order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat tends to curtail personal liberty of the judgment-debtors one of whom is lady. The liberty of judgment-debtor is not liable to be curtailed for realisation of the money without strictly adhering to the rules Rule 37 and Rule 40 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Besides, the detention of the petitioner no. 2 who is a woman is prohibited in execution of a decree for the payment of money according to section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the absence of any prescribed procedure in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 for execution of the decree the powers were conferred upon the Adalat to exercise jurisdiction applying the provision of Civil Procedure Code. But the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat manifestly abused his jurisdiction and passed the impugned order for detaining the judgment-debtors in civil prison including the petitioner no. 2 who is a woman. In Rule 37 and Rule 40 of the Order 21 C.P. Code the legislature consciously in case of arrest and detention of a judgment-debtor in a civil prison has incorporated the principle of audi alteram partem the age old principle of natural justice. The principle of natural justice is innate in the said two rules. Therefore, the impugned order has been made in violation of the principle of natural justice. The learned Artha Rin Adalat appears to have abused the jurisdiction conferred by law upon it and it has acted in excess of jurisdiction. Therefore, the order is liable to be struck down and it is struck down.
